conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for approximately 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower potential drawdowns. Expect steady, low-volatility performance.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and leveraged tech (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small positions.
Buy SLB at 4% as a new, strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure to leveraged assets while reducing overall concentration.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a new, high-quality setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and leveraged tech (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to 6% each.
Buy SLB at 6% as a new, strong scanner setup.
This plan aggressively leans into leverage and concentration for higher growth potential, accepting increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration, which amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Be aware of daily decay and rebalancing effects on leveraged ETFs, and maintain strict stop discipline as losses can accumulate rapidly.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Sell all other high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
income.read: This income plan aims for approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes reliable income and low drawdown by rotating into income-generating ETFs and cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
